topics.title: Apple
topics.hook: Apple was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne.
topics.explainer: Apple was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Technology Companies, Personalities, Brands and Products

connections.fact: Apple built an integrated Macintosh hardware-software platform, while Microsoft licensed Windows broadly to PC manufacturers.
Apple controls iOS and iPhone hardware together, whereas Android is used by Google and many independent device makers.

topics.title: Microsoft

connections.fact: Microsoft became dominant through software licensed across PC brands; Apple sold its own computers with its own operating system.
IBM selected Microsoft to provide the operating system for its original PC, helping Microsoft grow in personal computing.

connections.fact: Google acquired Android and leads development of the operating system and its major service ecosystem.
Google and Microsoft compete in web search, cloud services, browsers, and office software.

connections.fact: Amazon Web Services and IBM both sell computing infrastructure and services to organisations, though their company histories began in different markets.
Amazon and Google both operate cloud platforms and data-intensive online services, alongside their distinct commerce and search roots.

topics.title: IBM

connections.fact: IBM launched the IBM PC with a Microsoft-supplied operating system, linking an established hardware company to a young software vendor.

connections.relationship: Established enterprise vendor and cloud entrant
connections.fact: IBM's mainframe heritage contrasts with Amazon's internet-retail origin, yet both now serve enterprise computing workloads.

connections.fact: Android is the mobile operating system led by Google and distributed to many manufacturers.

connections.relationship: Open multi-vendor versus integrated mobile model
connections.fact: Android supports devices from many brands, while Apple restricts iOS to its own hardware ecosystem.

questions.q: Which three people founded Apple in 1976?
questions.explanation: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne formed Apple in 1976; Wayne soon sold his stake.

questions.q: Microsoft was founded in 1975 by which pair?
questions.explanation: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft in 1975 around software for early personal computers.

questions.q: PageRank research at Stanford is linked to the founders of which company?
questions.explanation: Larry Page and Sergey Brin developed the research that led to Google, with PageRank central to its early search approach.

questions.q: Which company began in 1994 as Jeff Bezos's online bookstore?
questions.explanation: Amazon started with online books before expanding into broad commerce, logistics, devices, media, and cloud services.

questions.q: A quiz clue mentions mainframes, enterprise computing, and a long research tradition. Which company fits?
questions.explanation: IBM is historically associated with enterprise hardware, especially mainframes, as well as corporate research.

options: Android is led by Google and used by many hardware makers
Android was IBM's original PC operating system
questions.explanation: Google leads Android development, and manufacturers across the industry use it on their mobile devices.
Among those choices Apple carries the 1976 founding date; Google and Amazon emerged in the 1990s.

questions.q: Why is IBM relevant to Microsoft's personal-computer rise?
options: IBM chose Microsoft to supply an operating system for the IBM PC
IBM created Android for Windows phones
questions.explanation: The operating-system deal for the IBM PC gave Microsoft software a pivotal place in the expanding PC market.
Android is the Google-led mobile platform; PageRank belongs to Google's origins, while Windows and iOS belong to Microsoft and Apple.

questions.q: A retailer later becomes a major provider of rented servers and storage. Which expansion is being described?
questions.explanation: Amazon Web Services extended Amazon beyond retail by offering on-demand computing infrastructure to other organisations.
